title: Protocol for reading and imaging live-cell PKA activity using ExRai-AKAR2
protocol: Determine the number of experimental conditions to be tested, denoted as X.
Include positive and negative controls in the setup: Fsk/IBMX treatment and no-treatment conditions.
Set up a total of X + 2 conditions on the plate reader assay.
Passage cells according to the experimental design and corresponding calculation.
Treat specific wells with Fsk (50 μM) and IBMX (100 μM) as positive controls.
Include non-treated wells as negative controls to ensure no significant baseline drifting during the assay.
Include a condition with non-transfected cells to correct for background fluorescence.
Calculate the total cell number for seeding based on the density of HEK293T cells.
Determine the quantity of plasmid DNA and PolyJet to be used for transfection according to the ratio specified.
Passage HEK293T cells for seeding and transfection as required.
Prepare boric acid buffer at a concentration of 50 mM boric acid, 25 mM sodium tetraborate, pH 8.5.
Dissolve poly-D-lysine (PDL) in the prepared buffer to achieve a final concentration of 0.1 mg/mL.
Add 50 μL of the PDL solution to each well designated for cell culture in a black-walled, clear-bottom 96-well assay plate.
Incubate the plates containing PDL-coated wells at 20°C–25°C for 24 hours.
Wash all wells once with HBSS after incubation.
Dilute calculated amount of ExRai-AKAR2 plasmid DNA into high-glucose DMEM to a concentration of 1 μg DNA/50 μL high-glucose DMEM.
Dilute calculated amount of PolyJet reagent into high-glucose DMEM to a concentration of 3 μL PolyJet/50 μL high-glucose DMEM.
Mix and incubate the DNA/lipid complex for 5 min at 20°C–25°C.
Harvest cultured HEK293T cells, collecting at least 5 × 10^4 × N cells.
Resuspend the harvested HEK293T cells in culture media to a final concentration of 5 × 10^4 cells/100 μL.
Prepare 3(X + 2) × 100 μL of cell suspension for transfection.
Prepare another 300 μL of cell suspension for the non-transfected control wells.
Transfect the cells by mixing 3(X + 2) × 100 μL of cell suspension with the DNA/lipid complex.
Seed both transfected and non-transfected cells by adding 100 μL of cell suspension into the corresponding wells of a PDL-coated 96-well plate.
Incubate the seeded cells for 24 h at 37°C to express the biosensor.
Check the fluorescence signal for the experimental groups and non-transfected controls 24 h after transfection.
Prepare 10× solutions of all drugs by diluting drug stocks with HBSS imaging buffer.
Set up the fluorescence microplate reader to perform dual-excitation measurements of ExRai-AKAR2 fluorescence intensity.
Set appropriate excitation and emission settings for fluorescence collection.
Use 480 nm excitation with a 10 nm bandwidth and 520 nm emission with a 20 nm bandwidth.
Apply 30 flashes and set camera gain to 180.
Read the plate using bottom-read mode.
Automatically determine the optimal Z position from a transfected well.
Acquire a baseline recording by reading the plate for one cycle.
Carefully remove culture media from each well.
Wash wells once with HBSS Imaging Buffer.
Refill each well with 45 μL of HBSS Imaging Buffer.
Remove the plate and add 5 μL of 10× drug solution to each well.
Assess the fluorescence of any new drug before inclusion in the assay using cells transfected by ExRai-AKAR2 (T/A).
Add 45 μL of Imaging Buffer for baseline read.
Add 5 μL of 10× drug solution or Imaging Buffer to read the fluorescence under 480-nm excitation/520-nm emission and 400-nm excitation/520-nm emission.
Re-insert the plate and resume reading for the desired number of cycles to obtain a time-course recording.
Repeat steps 24 and 25 for any subsequent drug additions.
Passage HEK293T cells into 35-mm glass-bottom dishes at approximately 30% confluency.
Determine the amount of ExRai-AKAR2 plasmid DNA and PolyJet to be used for transfection (500 ng DNA/1.5 μL PolyJet/35-mm dish).
Dilute the calculated amount of ExRai-AKAR2 plasmid DNA into high-glucose DMEM to a concentration of 500 ng DNA/50 μL high-glucose DMEM.
Dilute the calculated amount of PolyJet reagent into high-glucose DMEM to a concentration of 1.5 μL PolyJet/50 μL high-glucose DMEM.
Mix and incubate the DNA/lipid complex for 5 min at 20°C–25°C.
Transfect the cells by adding 100 μL of DNA/lipid complex into each 35-mm glass-bottom dish.
Incubate the cells for 24 h at 37°C to allow for protein expression.
Prepare drugs at a 1000× stock concentration.
Aliquot 2 μL of each 1000× drug stock into separate 1.5 mL tubes.
Store drug aliquots properly; typically on ice unless specified otherwise.
Perform real-time imaging with acute stimulation.
Use appropriate excitation and emission filters for dual-excitation imaging.
Set exposure times, ND filters, and acquisition intervals to optimize signal and prevent photobleaching.
For example, use a 480DF20 excitation filter and 535DF50 emission filter for the 488-nm channel (GFP480).
Use a 405DF20 excitation filter and 535DF50 emission filter for the 400-nm channel (GFP400).
Set exposure times to 500 ms for both channels.
Apply a 0.6 ND filter with acquisition intervals of 15–30 seconds.
Use high-magnification objectives (≥40×) for greater spatial resolution.
Aspirate the culture media from the imaging dish carefully.
Wash cells twice with 1 mL of HBSS Imaging Buffer.
Add 2 mL of Imaging Buffer for imaging.
Mount the prepared imaging dish on the microscope stage.
Focus the cells and begin acquiring images in both GFP480 and GFP400 channels.
Image the cells for at least 5 minutes prior to any stimulation to acquire a baseline signal.
Pause the image acquisition to perform the first drug addition.
Transfer approximately 0.5 mL of Imaging Buffer from the imaging dish into a 1.5 mL tube containing an aliquot of 1000× drug stock using a P1000 pipette.
Mix well by pipetting up and down.
Carefully add the mixture back to the imaging dish.
Gently mix within the imaging dish by pipetting at least 3 more times to ensure homogeneous distribution of the drug.
Mix drug aliquot into a smaller volume of Imaging Buffer using a P200 pipette.
Keep the pipette tip away from the center of the dish when adding the drug.
Avoid touching the imaging dish and microscope stage with the pipette tip to prevent shifting or loss of focus.
Resume imaging and continue acquisitions until the fluorescence signal reaches a plateau.
Repeat for any subsequent drug additions.
Perform Fsk/IBMX stimulation at the end of each imaging experiment as a positive control.
Test new and unknown compounds via epifluorescence imaging using ExRai-AKAR2 (T/A) mutant as a negative control.
Cells expressing ExRai-AKAR2 (T/A) should exhibit no ratio change in response to stimulation.
